months.summary: In August, the student will learn the foundational principles of algebra including variables, constants, and algebraic expressions. They will also focus on solving and graphing linear equations. This knowledge is essential as it forms the building blocks for more complex algebraic concepts they will encounter in the coming months.

During September, the student will explore systems of linear equations, learning to solve them using various methods like substitution and elimination. They will also study inequalities and absolute value equations, which will enhance their understanding of comparison and solutions to more complex equations.

In October, the focus will shift to polynomials, covering what they are and how to perform operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. The student will also learn how to factor polynomials, which is crucial for simplifying expressions and solving polynomial equations.

November is dedicated to rational expressions and equations. The student will learn how to simplify rational expressions and solve equations involving them. This is important for understanding more complicated algebraic concepts and how to handle variables in fractions.

In December, the studies will cover radicals and their functions. The student will learn how to simplify, add, subtract, multiply, and divide radical expressions and how to solve radical equations. This knowledge will help them understand how to work with roots in various mathematical scenarios.

January focuses on quadratic functions. The student will learn different forms of quadratics, including vertex form and standard form, as well as how to factor quadratics. Understanding these concepts is critical for tackling higher-level mathematics.

In February, the student will delve deeper into quadratic equations. They will learn to use the quadratic formula for solving equations and how to graph quadratic functions. This will enhance their ability to interpret and analyze the behavior of quadratic functions.

March introduces exponential functions and their properties. The student will learn how to express equations in exponential form and solve various exponential equations. This topic is significant as it lays the groundwork for understanding logarithmic functions.

In April, the student will focus on logarithmic functions. They will study their properties and learn how to solve logarithmic equations. This will deepen their understanding of the relationship between exponents and logarithms, which is essential for advanced mathematics.

May is reserved for reviewing major topics covered throughout the year. The student will prepare for an algebra exam while also applying what they have learned to real-life problems. This consolidation phase ensures they are well-prepared for future studies and practical applications.
